overview: Second year is the foundational pillar of Computer Science. This year decides your placement readiness and technical depth. Master Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA), Object-Oriented Programming (OOP in Java/C++), Database Management Systems (DBMS & SQL), Operating Systems (OS), and Computer Architecture.
keyGoals: Master Data Structures (Arrays, LinkedLists, Stacks, Queues, Trees, Heaps, Graphs).
Solve 150+ DSA problems on LeetCode / GeeksforGeeks across standard patterns.
Master Relational Databases (PostgreSQL / MySQL, ACID properties, Indexing, Normalization).
Deep dive into Operating Systems (Processes, Threads, Concurrency, Virtual Memory, Deadlocks).
Build 2 full-stack database-backed applications with CRUD APIs.

subjects.name: Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA)
subjects.importance: Critical - #1 Subject evaluated in all software company interviews
coreConcepts: Asymptotic Time & Space Complexity (Big-O, Big-Theta, Big-Omega)
Linear Structures: Arrays, Dynamic Arrays, Singly & Doubly Linked Lists
Stack & Queue: Monotonic Stack, Circular Queue, Deque
Non-linear: Binary Trees, Binary Search Trees (BST), AVL & Red-Black Trees, Binary Heaps
Hashing & Hash Tables: Collision Resolution (Chaining, Open Addressing)
Graphs: Adjacency Matrix/List, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Prim's & Kruskal's MST
Algorithm Paradigms: Divide & Conquer, Greedy, Dynamic Programming (DP), Backtracking

subjects.name: Database Management Systems (DBMS & SQL)
subjects.importance: Critical - Required in all backend, fullstack, and systems roles
coreConcepts: Relational Model & Relational Algebra
Advanced SQL: Joins, Subqueries, Aggregations, Group By, CTEs, Window Functions
Entity-Relationship (ER) Modeling & Schema Design
Functional Dependencies & Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF)
ACID Properties & Transaction Management (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability)
Concurrency Control (2PL, Timestamp Ordering, Deadlock Prevention)
Database Indexing (B-Trees, B+ Trees, Hash Indexing) & Query Optimization

subjects.name: Operating Systems (OS)
subjects.importance: High - Fundamental for writing concurrent, performant backend code
coreConcepts: Processes vs Threads, Context Switching, Process Control Block (PCB)
CPU Scheduling Algorithms (FCFS, SJF, Round Robin, Multi-Level Feedback Queue)
Inter-Process Communication (IPC: Pipes, Message Queues, Shared Memory)
Process Synchronization: Race Conditions, Critical Section, Mutex Locks, Semaphores
Deadlocks: Necessary Conditions (Coffman), Banker's Algorithm, Deadlock Recovery
Memory Management: Paging, Segmentation, Virtual Memory, Page Replacement (LRU, FIFO, Clock)
File Systems: Inodes, Directory Structure, Disk Scheduling (SCAN, C-LOOK)

recommendedProjects.title: Library Book Management & Fine Calculation System
recommendedProjects.problemStatement: Manage library circulation: book inventory, membership tier validation, borrowing limits, automated return date tracking, and overdue fine computation.
keyFeatures: 3NF normalized database schema (Books, Authors, Copies, Members, BorrowTransactions).
ACID compliant borrowing transaction (checks book availability, decrements copy count, creates borrow log).
Automated overdue fine computation with configurable grace periods.
Reports: Most borrowed books, active defaulters, overdue alerts.

recommendedProjects.title: Interactive OS Process Scheduling & Memory Simulator
recommendedProjects.problemStatement: Students struggle to visualize how CPU schedulers and page replacement algorithms behave under concurrent workloads.
keyFeatures: Live visual simulation of CPU scheduling algorithms (FCFS, Round Robin with customizable time quantum, Priority, SJF).
Dynamic Gantt chart rendering with real-time Waiting Time and Turnaround Time metrics calculation.
Virtual memory page replacement simulator (FIFO, LRU, Optimal) showing Page Hit/Fault ratios.

recommendedProjects.title: Full-Stack Task & Bug Tracking Board (Jira / Trello Clone)
recommendedProjects.problemStatement: Engineering teams need a visual kanban board to manage sprint tasks, assign bugs, attach labels, and track status transitions (To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done).
keyFeatures: User authentication with JWT (Login, Registration, Role-based Access: Admin, Developer).
Task filtering by assignee, priority (P0, P1, P2), tags, and sprint deadline.
Activity audit log tracking every status change and comment.
learningOutcomes: State management with React Context / Redux

recommendedProjects.title: CLI In-Memory Key-Value Store with TTL (Redis-Lite)
recommendedProjects.problemStatement: Build a lightweight in-memory cache server that supports key-value retrieval, expiration timeouts (TTL), and LRU eviction policy.
keyFeatures: Core commands: `SET key value [EX seconds]`, `GET key`, `DEL key`, `EXISTS key`.
Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction algorithm when memory limit is exceeded (O(1) Hash Map + Doubly Linked List).
Background cleaner thread / timer removing expired TTL keys.
Simple TCP socket listener allowing connection via `telnet` or `nc`.

recommendedProjects.title: Shortest Path & Metro Route Finder (Graph Algorithm Visualizer)
recommendedProjects.problemStatement: Given a network of transit stations, interchange lines, and train schedules, find the shortest route by distance or time.
keyFeatures: Weighted graph representation of metro lines and transfer stations.
Dijkstra algorithm finding shortest path between Source and Destination.
Calculates ticket fare based on distance and station hops.
Interactive visual path rendering highlighting the optimal route.

recommendedTopicSequence: 5. Binary Search on Arrays & Answer Spaces (15 Qs)
6. Binary Trees & BST (Inorder, Preorder, Postorder, Level Order) (25 Qs)
7. Binary Heap & Priority Queues / Top-K elements (10 Qs)
8. Graphs (BFS, DFS, Cycle Detection, Topological Sort, Dijkstra) (20 Qs)
9. Dynamic Programming (1D, 2D Grid, Knapsack, LCS, LIS) (30 Qs)
